chunks: From him, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Zayd ibn al-Jahm al-Hilali, from Malik ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man shakes the hand of his companion, the one who necessitates the handshake has greater reward than the one who waits (for it). Indeed, and the sins fall away between them until no sin remains.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for initiating a handshake in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the handshake (Mushaafaha) as a recommended act (Mustahabb) that fosters social cohesion and spiritual purification. It specifically elevates the status of the initiator, suggesting that proactive engagement in greeting carries superior merit, while the mutual exchange serves as a mechanism for the shedding of minor sins, reinforcing the concept of interpersonal mercy in daily interactions.
